Keep each student focused on one achievable output. Use the checkpoints below to turn a progress update into a clear decision.

:::

::: {.section-heading}
## A useful supervision meeting in three moves
:::

::: {.three-grid}
::: {.instruction-card}
### 01 · See the evidence
Open the task issue and linked draft PR. Ask the student to show the actual output, version record, and anything that failed.
:::
::: {.instruction-card}
### 02 · Make a decision
Record “ready for next step”, “revise”, or “blocked”, with a short reason. Keep scientific review separate from a successful website build.
:::
::: {.instruction-card}
### 03 · Set the next action
Agree one output, an owner, and a target date. Add it to the issue so both of you leave with the same plan.
:::
:::

## Review checkpoints

::: {.checkpoint-table}

| Stage | Ask to see | Decision to make |
|---|---|---|
| **Define** | Question, fixed dataset version, access conditions, acceptance criteria | Is the scope achievable and appropriate? |
| **Inspect** | One-scan manifest, metadata, and quality notes | Is the input suitable for the proposed method? |
| **Process** | Environment, command, exit status, logs, and overlays | Is the pilot acceptable? Agree QC rules before scaling. |
| **Measure** | Region table, units, provenance, and identifier audit | Are the measures and participant joins correct? |
| **Analyse** | Model plan, assumptions, exclusions, uncertainty, and figures | Are the claims supported and limitations clear? |
| **Share** | Reproduction steps, output locations, permissions, and known failures | Can the next student reproduce the accepted work? |

:::

::: {.workspace-grid}
::: {.workspace-main}

Copy this into the task issue or PR. Put confidential feedback in your approved private channel.

### Before the placement starts

- Agree the question and first milestone.
- Confirm repository and dataset access.
- Choose one primary compute route.
- Agree a meeting schedule and storage location.
- Explain what can be shared publicly.

[View the student experience →](student.qmd)
:::
:::
:::

## Keep the cohort organised

Use one bounded GitHub issue per task. Assign a student, record the target date, and link the draft PR. A GitHub Project can group issues into **Todo → In progress → In review → Done**. Link your cohort’s Project from its coordination issue once created.

Avoid participant identifiers, restricted outputs, and confidential student assessments in this public repository. [Review the contribution workflow](CONTRIBUTING.md) and [handover requirements](projects/structural-mri-handover.qmd).
